quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other motorists that you are riding near them.
Help other motorists see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other motorists that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other motorists that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Use your brake light to communicate with other drivers. Flash your brake light when slowing down for a sharp turn on a high-speed road or when stopping where drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves again.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you approach an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Always slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet on. Use hearing protection on every ride to protect your ears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: How do convex mirrors differ from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make approaching vehicles look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's, especially when the taillight is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light clearly.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat, your steering will suddenly feel:
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Helmets are:
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has white background with red and black markings. This sign tells you that you cannot turn right.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions while riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must:

options.text: Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear views to the sides, fasten securely, let air flow to prevent fogging, and fit eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which is not a common type of helmet?
questions.explanation: The two main types of motorcycle helmets are three-quarter and full-face. Full-face helmets give the best protection.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect your riding ability?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can hurt your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: For motorcycle operators, helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards when you operate a motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get better grip for your tires.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Has no impact on safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may signal the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than using either alone.
Can be stronger than using either alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. Some drugs become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip. Use only the rear brake to slow down while turning.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip. What does this mean?

options.text: It usually gives good traction, unless it is raining.
You should only ride on it if another vehicle is in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually gives good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually has enough traction for safe riding, unless it is raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide. Riders can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Why does a motorcycle rider have an advantage over a car driver when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: A motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
A rider can move to the left side of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
Motorcycles can stop faster than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: A rider can move to the left side of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
questions.explanation: When parked vehicles are on your right, you can ride on the left side of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, drivers getting out, or people stepping between cars. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How should you cross angled railroad tracks?

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight across in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across in your lane.
questions.explanation: It is usually safest to ride straight across angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your angle may move you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which lane position best stops other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane

questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you. When riding behind a car, the center position also makes you more visible in the car's rearview mirror, where the driver is more likely to see you.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be in a group?

options.text: At the front leading the group
Near the front of the group
At the back of the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, behind the leader. This way, more experienced riders can lead and watch the less experienced riders at the same time.
